analysis.title: North America Metals & Mining - Sunday Morning Metals: Earnings Highlights (2026-11-01)
key_insights: Earnings largely wind down this week. LEU (Neutral) and MP (Overweight) report Thursday. JPM expects LEU margins to be pressured by the loss of the cost-plus HALEU operations contract and mix, with updates on the Westerman acquisition and incremental derisking.

JPM expects MP earnings to be pressured by lagged 2Q maintenance-related costs. Commentary should focus on initial commercial magnet sales, heavies/recycling midstream operations and restarting on-site chlor-alkali facilities.

NUE 3Q was in-line with record mill shipments. Tubular shipments rose 82% Y/Y, and J&D pricing rose $110/t Q/Q vs. $20/t at STLD. FCF was about $1.6B, the highest since 3Q23, an implied ~11% annualized yield vs. ~8% for STLD.

NUE reiterated FY26 shipments +10% Y/Y, implying a 4Q step down from seasonality, fewer fiscal days and planned maintenance. Earnings were guided 'in-line or modestly higher', and investors view the 4Q guide as conservative.

FCX 3Q beat, but FY26 and FY27 copper sales were cut by about 100Kt each (-3% and -2%) on weather disruptions and mine sequencing. FY26 production costs were raised 2% to $3.29/lb. Bagdad FID is targeted for 4Q26 with the ~$4.5B budget reiterated.
FCX commercial-scale additive (leaching) trials are on track for 1H27. If successful, they could lift the run-rate toward ~300Mlbs by FYE27, a target moved from FYE26.

CSTM 3Q beat with a guidance raise. FY26 EBITDA guide rose 5% to $1.03-1.06B, implying 4Q EBITDA of $193M (-45% Q/Q, -12% vs. Bloomberg consensus) on seasonality, downtime and weaker mix. JPM upgraded CSTM to OW using a 6.5x multiple vs. 7.5x for peer KALU.
TECK 3Q beat on Trail profitability and strong by-products despite severe weather. QB2 production missed by 12% (-15% Q/Q) but had no TMF-related downtime. Management tightened FY26 guidance.

AEM 3Q beat but cost guidance moved toward the high end on a revised production plan, retaliatory Canadian tariffs (~$5/oz) and cost inflation (diesel est. +$65/oz). AEM now targets 50% of FY26 FCF for shareholder returns, up from 40%.

US and Canada reportedly discuss easing S232 steel/auto tariffs, with a possible deal before the November 3 midterms. JPM says the import arbitrage for Canadian HRC stays closed even at a 25% rate, so US steel markets see minimal impact.

US mills are tightening 2027 contract terms. HRC/HDG discounts are being cut to 2%-3.5% from 6%-8% for 2026, rebates are removed in some cases and volumes are reduced. JPM calls it a sellers market that should benefit domestic mills.

Canada gave Cleveland-Cliffs 15 days to restore Stelco jobs or justify layoffs tied to Hamilton Works idling, with court remedies, penalties or forced divestment possible. Cliffs says Stelco is in full compliance, and the CEO says Stelco is not for sale. JPM reads it as a push for tougher trade policy on value-add products.
Centrus shipped its first new centrifuge ahead of its year-end target. JPM calls it a de-risking milestone but keeps LEU at Neutral because the ramp is long-dated and the AI risk-off tape persists.

Constellation received a conditional $5B DOE loan commitment supporting nuclear upgrades adding about 1.1 GW. JPM sees it as a constructive long-term signal for uranium and enrichment demand, with timing dependent on project execution.

GM terminated its VAC rare-earth magnet sourcing agreement with the US unit of Energy Fuels, removing ~90% of planned offtake for VAC's South Carolina plant, and the parties are in arbitration. GM's legacy ~1Ktpa supply deal with MP is in qualification with first commercial shipments imminent.
NRC accepted General Matter's first license application in about half the typical review time. General Matter plans to submit a HALEU license amendment next year.
Rio Tinto is set to restart underground mining at Oyu Tolgoi after a seismic-triggered rockfall. JPM estimates ~410Kt of copper output this year and 470Kt in 2027, about 1.5% of global mined supply.

JPM's nuclear note says equities de-rated sharply in 2026 on momentum unwind, data center opposition and higher rates. JPM sees an investable framework forming around bipartisan federal support, state funding, foreign capital and hyperscaler engagement.

JPM's rates note says higher rates risk about 75% of US steel demand (50% non-residential construction, 25% auto), but non-residential impacts come with a lag and infrastructure and data center projects may be insulated. Gold lost about $17/oz per 1bp rise in 10Y real yields from March to July 2026.

JPM's uranium model forecasts a slight primary supply deficit in CY27-28E, a surplus in CY30-35E and a structural deficit after CY35. Term prices reached ~US$96/lb by end-September while spot traded sideways. Uranium equities price at or below spot (US$90/lb) and JPM's long-term US$85/lb.

LME Week feedback on copper tilted cautious, centered on US tariff inaction unwinding some of the metal's dislocation premium. Aluminum has a strong bearish medium-term consensus on expected oversupply, though the market is tight for now.
US HRC lead times are elevated. SMU's rose to 9.5 weeks from 9.1 and Platts' held at 9.2, vs. a normal 4-6 weeks.

Investor sentiment: AA trades at 3.6x FY27 spot EV/EBITDA vs. a 5.0x historical average. RS investors debate how much volume and share is needed to hold earnings once DHS border wall contributions fade in FY28. CRS investors debate when to re-engage given no catalysts. Lithium sentiment turned more bearish on supply after the prospect of a Jianxiawo restart.

tension_points.bull_case: Non-residential impacts come with a lag, and infrastructure and megatrend projects (data center, energy infra, border wall) may be relatively insulated.
tension_points.bear_case: Elevated US rates typically handicap industrial and auto demand and delay capital investment, a risk to about 75% of US steel demand.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Rate hikes typically lead non-residential construction spending by 18-24 months, so the lagged hit would show up in non-residential spending.

tension_points.bull_case: Underlying copper fundamentals remain generally supportive.
tension_points.bear_case: US tariff inaction could unwind some of the metal's dislocation premium.

tension_points.bull_case: A new nuclear compact among federal, state, foreign capital and hyperscalers could make the trade investable, and data center, electrification and onshoring load growth returns to new nuclear.
tension_points.bear_case: Equities de-rated sharply in 2026 on data center demand questions, FOAK-to-NOAK execution risk, long construction timelines and uncertain capital costs.
